The structure of Ca2Fe8O16 (reduced formula Ca(FeO2)4) crystallizes in the monoclinic space group C2/c (No. 15), with 26 atoms per unit cell distributed over four independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Fe centers in octahedral environments with six O neighbors, while Ca centers adopt a 12-neighbor, close-packed-like local arrangement. The FeO6 octahedra share corners and edges with one another, and corner-sharing also occurs between FeO6 octahedra and Ca-centered 12-vertex polyhedra. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component.
